name: Discipline Levels
intro: Every discipline levels up on its own as you use it. Higher levels unlock its skills and give [proficiency points](mechanic:proficiency-points) for its passives.

sections.heading: How They Level
paragraphs: Every discipline starts at level 1, and there is no level cap. Melee weapons get experience when you hit an enemy, [Shields](discipline:shields) when you block an attack, [Unarmed](discipline:unarmed) when you punch, and magic disciplines when you cast their spells.

sections.heading: The Skill Tree
paragraphs: Press L to open the skill tree. You unlock skills and buy passives there. Tab opens the radial menu, which also has a Skill Tree button.

evidence: Run facts1, build 24464547: on a new character every discipline and profession was at level 1, with 0 skill points and 0 proficiency points.
Run progression2, build 24464547: Necromancy passed level 5,700 without stopping.

Code: Goblin_Base's Damage From Player Melee calls the player's Add Proper Weapon EXP, FirstPersonCharacter2's Block Attack calls Increase Shield EXP, the fist animation's AnimNotify_SwingFist calls Unarmed Level Tracking, and Skill's Add EXP Based On Spell Type passes a spell's experience to its magic discipline.
Run facts1, build 24464547: IMC_InGameActions maps L to IA_OpenCloseSkillTree and Tab to IA_OpenCloseRadialMenu. Run radial1: the radial menu shows Skill Tree with L beside it.

name: Skill Points
intro: Skill points unlock skills in the skill trees. You get one each time your character levels up.

sections.heading: How You Get Them
paragraphs: You get 1 skill point each time your character levels up. Leveling a discipline, such as [Pyromancy](discipline:pyromancy), gives no skill points.

sections.heading: How You Spend Them
paragraphs: Each skill costs 1 skill point. You can unlock it once you reach the level its skill tree shows for it. Click the skill again to get the point back.

evidence: Run progression2, build 24464547: each character level up added 1 to Skill Points.
Runs grants1 and progression3, build 24464547: discipline level ups left Skill Points unchanged.
Run passives1, build 24464547: unlocking a skill took 1 skill point, and pressing it again returned it.

name: Proficiency Points
intro: Proficiency points buy passives. Each discipline has its own, which you get by leveling that discipline.

sections.heading: How You Get Them
paragraphs: Each time a discipline levels up, you get proficiency points for that discipline. Focuses and Vampirism have no passives, so their points buy nothing.

rows: 1 for the first level up, then none

sections.heading: How You Spend Them
paragraphs: A passive costs points of its own discipline. A passive with ranks costs more for each rank you buy. Lasting Servitude costs 2 points for its first rank, then 4, 6, 8 and 10, so all five ranks cost 30.
Each discipline page lists what every rank of its passives costs.

evidence: Run grants1, build 24464547: a discipline level up added 1 proficiency point of that discipline, Necromancy 2, Focuses, whose level the game names Staff, 1 for its first level up and none after, and Vampirism none. Run progression3 also saw Vampirism's first two level ups add none.
Run passives1, build 24464547: Lasting Servitude's ranks cost 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 points, and Lingering Souls' 1 to 5.

name: Blood Levels
intro: Blood Levels is a video setting that changes how much blood you see and how many [Blood Magic](discipline:blood-magic) points you get. To change it, open Settings from the pause menu and choose Video and Effect Settings.

sections.heading: Blood Magic Points
paragraphs: Each time Blood Magic levels up, your Blood Magic points are set to the number for your setting. They replace the points you had, so points you saved are lost.

sections.heading: Getting the Most Points
paragraphs: Set Blood Levels to BLOODBATH before Blood Magic levels up, and spend your points before its next level.

evidence: Run rowgate1, build 24464547: with the settings window set to No blood, A bit of blood, Default Amount and BLOODBATH, the next Blood Magic level up left 2, 3, 4 and 6 points, and after spending 2 of 3 points a level up restored 3.
Code: Blood Magic Level Tracking sets the points to the game instance's Blood Level plus 1, which SettingsWindow1's Blood selection writes.

name: World Map Events
intro: World map events are the ambushes, camps, animals and gathering spots that appear around you while you travel the world map.

sections.heading: How Events Appear
paragraphs: While you travel, a new event appears near you about every 5 seconds until 7 are on the map.
The terrain around you decides which events can appear. Each event disappears after a while unless you enter it.
While you stand still, no new event appears and the events on the map do not run out.
Entering an event takes you to a camp area nearby. The Hostile Logging Camp has its own area. A Merchant Caravan trades with you on the world map, and an Airship is boarded there.

sections.heading: Terrain
paragraphs: Every terrain uses one of five lists of events. Look up the terrain you are in to see which.

evidence: Code: TopDownCharacter_Working's Spawn Overworld Event Actor spawns an event with a 35% chance per frame while fewer than 7 exist, and Cooldown Overworld Event Spawn blocks the next for 5 seconds.
Code: Overworld_EventActor's Select Location Data Table picks the list by the nearest terrain tag, Select Event draws by weight, and Choose Actor to Spawn sets how long the event stays.
Code: SmallEventSpawner's Recieve Event spawns the creatures of the event the player entered.

Runs events1 and events2, build 24464547: the moving pawn saw at most 7 live events in Pine Forest over 90 seconds per run. A stationary pawn had no new event in 90 seconds. Calling Enter Event on a Goblin Boar Riders actor opened a pine forest camp with 4 mounted goblins. Setting the save tag directly gave 1 Bear or 6 Wild Wolves in that camp.

name: Calendar Events
intro: Calendar events change one area for a day, with more enemies, falling meteors, a ghost ship or better harvests. The game schedules events about two weeks ahead.

sections.heading: How Events Are Chosen
paragraphs: A day has at most one event. For each day the game chooses one of 18 areas at random and then an event that can happen there. Soulfaring Night, on Vohath 15 of 874, gets none.
Open Calendar on the world map and check a date for the event and its area. Your Character Sheet also has a Calendar button.
The event happens while you are in its area on its day.

sections.heading: Events
paragraphs: Chance per Day is how likely a day's event is this one, in any of its areas.

sections.heading: Calendar Areas
paragraphs: Calendar events can happen in these areas.

evidence: Code: CalendarEventManager's Generate Event gives each free date within its Foresight Range of 14 days one event, and Assemble Event For Given Location picks one of 18 area names at random and draws by EventSpawnRate among the rows of CalendarEventInfo that name the area or ALL.
Code: CalendarEvent_Spawner's Recieve Event calls the function of the day's event, such as Spawn Ghost Ship.

Runs events1 and events2, build 24464547: each fresh calendar had 13 generated entries on Vohath 2 through 14, all in eligible areas. Setting the date to Vohath 7 before opening Parford Lake gave 25 Rabbits for its scheduled Rabbit Swarm, versus 0 on Vohath 1. Runs events2 and holidays2 generated an event on Vohath 25 but not Vohath 15.

Run review-interface, build 24464547: the world map's Calendar button opened the calendar with event and area names on their dates. The Character Sheet's Calendar button also opened the calendar, but the sheet covered it in that capture.
